findings.title: Core well name: "Telepea 2" vs "Telopea 2"
findings.detail: The core-photo metadata statement lists "Tinchoo Play (Telepea 2)". The panel caption (OCR 0.91) and the GA boreholes layer both read TELOPEA 2.

findings.title: Play name: "Tinchoo Play" vs "Nappamerri Play"
findings.detail: The metadata statement calls the panel "Tinchoo Play"; the panel header and the GA Cooper chart call the interval "Nappamerri Play".
findings.fix: Map "Tinchoo Play" as an alternate label (synonym) of Nappamerri Play.

findings.title: Granite wash base depth: 3,044.04 m (caption) vs 3,044.02 m (report)
findings.detail: Panel TEGI-66241-3 prints 3,044.04 m (OCR 0.92); the data guide (p.4) states 3,042.21–3,044.02 m from Moomba 236.
findings.fix: Keep both with provenance; flag for curator.

findings.title: McKinlay Member depths run upward: 1,452.6 m → 1,452.37 m
findings.detail: Panel TEGI-66241-9 labels the first column 1,452.6 m (top) to 1,452.37 m (base); likely 1,452.06 m.
findings.fix: Hold value; send to curator (likely missing zero).

findings.title: Scale bar reads "1 cm" on panels 9 and 10
findings.detail: All other panels show a 1 m scale bar; panels TEGI-66241-9 and -10 show "1 cm" although the depth labels span ~0.3 m per column.

findings.title: Warburton metadata titled "Lake Eyre Basin Extent"
findings.detail: The metadata statement for the Warburton Basin extent has DATASET TITLE = "Lake Eyre Basin Extent" while its abstract describes the Warburton Basin.

findings.title: Declared extent does not match the data (15 of 15 metadata statements)
findings.detail: Every metadata statement declares the same box 139.87–141.46°E, 27.63–28.48°S (about 1.6° × 0.85°). The Cooper Basin outline actually spans 139.37–143.97°E, 24.52–29.42°S.
findings.fix: Replace declared extents with extents computed from geometry (auto geo-tagging).

findings.title: Cooper Basin age: 304–237 Ma (data guide) vs 318–230 Ma (provinces record)
findings.detail: Table 1 of the data guide gives Gzhelian (304 Ma) to Ladinian (237 Ma). The Australian Geological Provinces attributes delivered with the basin outline give 318 Ma (Late Carboniferous) to 230 Ma (Triassic).
findings.fix: Keep both with provenance; prefer the newer data guide (2023) after curator review.

findings.title: Structure names differ between layers: Momay/Morney, Canway/Canaway, Warbrecah/Warbreccan
findings.detail: The structures layer spells "Momay Anticline", "Canway Ridge" and "Warbrecah Anticline"; the annotation layer (and the faults/boreholes layers) use "Morney", "Canaway" and "Warbreccan".
findings.fix: Merge as one entity with alternate labels after curator approval.

findings.title: Operator names vary across the 3D seismic layer
findings.detail: The same companies appear as e.g. "Santos Ltd" / "SANTOS LIMITED" and "Beach Petroleum" / "BEACH PETROLEUM LIMITED" / "Beach Energy".

crossChecks.check: MSL DEPTH against KB DEPTH and the printed Z(KB)
CORR. TIME reproduced from RECORD TIME (straight-ray slant correction, reconstructed; the method is not printed)
crossChecks.formula: CORR ≈ RECORD × z / √(z² + 300²) − 36, with z = KB DEPTH − 18 − 6 ft (KB−GL = 179 − 161 = 18 ft; SOURCE DEPTH 6; OFFSET 300 ft)
crossChecks.result: 73 of 73 rows reproduce the printed CORR. TIME to the nearest ms. The datum shot also fits: 77 × 155/√(155²+300²) = 35.3 ms vs printed 35.

crossChecks.check: INTERVAL VELOCITY against the printed depths and times
crossChecks.formula: INTERVAL VELOCITY = ΔMSL DEPTH / ΔCORR. TIME (ft/s, times in s)
crossChecks.result: 71 of 73 values agree after rounding (e.g. shot 74: 170 ft / 0.026 s = 6538). Exceptions: shot 43 prints 8125 where the row values give 68/0.008 = 8500; shot 37 has the same time as shot 2 (556 ms), so its printed 7857 is a carry-over.

crossChecks.check: RMS VELOCITY against the printed interval velocities
crossChecks.result: 71 of 73 values reproduce within ±1 ft/s from the row above. Shot 43 prints 7522 (expected ~7498) and shot 42 prints 7569 (expected ~7549); the bold overtyping on shot 43 suggests a hand correction that was not carried through.

crossChecks.check: Are the table times one-way or two-way?
crossChecks.result: Not labelled: headers read only "ARRIVAL TIME ms", "CORR. TIME ms", "RECORD TIME" and "CORR. TIME". The values behave as one-way vertical times below MSL: the printed interval velocities use them directly, and Enclosure 2 plots them at 2 × CORR. TIME on its TWO-WAY TIME axis.

crossChecks.check: Survey elevations against the completion report
crossChecks.result: Z(KB) 179 ft vs KB 181.9 ft: −2.9 ft. Z(GL) 161 ft vs GL 160.3 ft: +0.7 ft. For the same KB depth, the table's MSL depth is 2.9 ft deeper than a conversion with 181.9 ft.

crossChecks.check: Two-way time at top Toolachee from the checkshot table
crossChecks.formula: Top Toolachee = 6326 − 181.9 = 6144.1 ft MSL. Bracketing shots by depth: shot 3 (6139 ft, 715 ms) and shot 14 (6208 ft, 718 ms). t = 715 + (6144.1 − 6139)/(6208 − 6139) × (718 − 715) = 715.22 ms one-way; TWT = 2t
crossChecks.result: 1.430 s TWT (715.2 ms one-way, CORR. TIME). Sensitivity: shot 3 is out of trend, and interpolating shots 15 (6116 ft, 709 ms) and 14 instead gives 1.423 s. Using the table's own KB (6326 − 179 = 6147 ft MSL) gives 1.431 s.

crossChecks.result: Report 6526 ft KB = 6344.1 ft MSL; diagram 6387 ft MSL; diagram minus report = +42.9 ft. Mismatch of 43 ft. The report's Patchawarra depth instead matches the diagram's MURTEREE top: 6526 − 179 = 6347 (diagram -6347'). The completion-report read lists no Murteree pick.

crossChecks.check: Two-way time at top Toolachee: T-Z curve vs checkshot table
crossChecks.formula: Curve read at 6144.1 ft MSL; Δ = curve − table = 1.4288 − 1.4304 s
crossChecks.result: Curve 1.429 s vs table 1.430 s (shots 3 and 14): −1.6 ms, inside the ±3 ms reading precision of the faint deep curve. At the diagram's own Toolachee depth (6147 ft) the curve also reads 1.429 s. Interpolating shots 15 and 14 instead gives 1.423 s, 5.3 ms earlier than the curve.

crossChecks.check: Checkshot table points vs the × marks on Enclosure 2
crossChecks.formula: × expected at (2 × CORR. TIME, MSL DEPTH); offsets = diagram − table
crossChecks.result: 72 of 73 marks found within ±2.6 ms and ±9 ft; median offset +1.8 ms and −1.6 ft (consistent, small; cause not shown). Marks for shots 2/37 (12 ft apart, same time) and 12/4 (4 ft apart) overlap and cannot be separated. Shot 3 plots off the curve, matching its out-of-trend time in the table.

crossChecks.check: Checkshot shot 36: depth on the diagram
crossChecks.result: × plotted at about 4237 ft MSL, 1.127 s vs table 4262 ft, 1.126 s: −25 ft. The table row is internally consistent (KB 4441 − 179 = 4262; both neighbouring interval velocities reproduce).

crossChecks.check: Formation-tagged checkshots vs diagram tops (same datum, KB 179)
crossChecks.result: Shot 2 'Transition Beds' 4175 vs TRANSITION 4175: 0 ft. Shot 4 'Patchawarra Formation' 6386 vs PATCHAWARRA 6387: +1 ft. Shot 5 'Pre-Permian' 6881 vs PRE-PERMIAN 6882: +1 ft. Shot 3 'Toolachee Formation' 6139 vs TOOLACHEE 6147: +8 ft, so shot 3 sits 8 ft above the diagram's own Toolachee top.

crossChecks.check: What the circles measure: V.S.P.–sonic difference vs the gap between × marks and the curve
crossChecks.formula: (checkshot TWT − curve TWT) / 2 compared with the circle value at the same level
crossChecks.result: At 27 cleanly separated levels (170–4187 ft), 25 agree within ±1.5 ms (median −0.9 ms); the outlier is the shallowest level, 170 ft (−5 ms). This supports reading the solid line as the sonic-derived T-Z curve and the circles as V.S.P. minus sonic one-way time.

crossChecks.result: Curve ends at about 6960 ft and 1.550 s; shot 6 ("Bottom of hole") is 6955 ft and 1.552 s.

benchmarks.q: Which source defines the Cooper Basin play intervals, and how many play intervals does it use?
benchmarks.key: The Geoscience Australia Cooper Basin data guide (TEGI, 2023): the succession is divided into 16 play intervals; the play table lists 16 named plays from the Merrimelia Play to the Cenozoic Play.

benchmarks.q: According to the Cooper Basin data guide, how many boreholes lie within the geological extent of the basin, and how much 2D seismic supports the interpretation?
benchmarks.key: 4,879 boreholes; 147,801 line km of 2D seismic (and 29,896 km² of 3D seismic).

benchmarks.q: Which figure in the Cooper Basin data guide shows where the boreholes and seismic surveys are, and on which page?
benchmarks.key: Figure 2, on page 2: the distribution of 2D seismic survey lines, 3D seismic surveys and borehole locations in the Cooper Basin region and surrounds.

benchmarks.q: Which Adavale Basin units are recorded as reservoirs in the play table, and which carry a tight-gas flag?
benchmarks.key: Reservoirs: Buckabie Formation; Etonvale Formation; Lissoy Sandstone; Eastwood Formation; Gumbardo Formation. Tight gas: Buckabie Formation, Lissoy Sandstone.

benchmarks.q: Where is the North Bowen Basin floor deepest, and how deep does it get?
benchmarks.key: The Taroom Trough: about 10,046 m to the basin floor (computed from the GA depth-to-basement grid).

evidence.doc: Depth to Basement North Bowen Basin (GA grid)

benchmarks.q: What is the mean maximum horizontal stress (SHmax) direction inside the Cooper Basin, from quality A–C records, and how many records support it?
benchmarks.key: About N100°E (99.7°) from 73 quality A–C records inside the basin (130 in total). Only 6 of the 73 state a regime (5 strike-slip, 1 thrust), so the regime is weakly constrained.

benchmarks.q: Rank the closest analogs in other basins to the Cooper Basin Patchawarra Play (Permian, fluvio-lacustrine sandstone with coal) and justify the top choice with evidence.
benchmarks.key: Default weights rank the Aramac Play (Galilee Basin) first, score 51.1. A good answer cites the play table rows for age, environment and lithology, and notes that petroleum roles are not recorded for the Cooper units. The hypothesis test shows the gaps: roles are not recorded for the Patchawarra, and the resource flags differ (coal seam gas in the Aramac, none in the Patchawarra).

benchmarks.q: What is the top of the Toolachee Formation in Marabooka 1, below the kelly bushing and below sea level?
benchmarks.key: 6326 ft below KB (1928.16 m). With KB 181.9 ft, that is 6144.1 ft below sea level (computed). The velocity chart (Enclosure 2) shows the top at 6,147 ft below sea level because the velocity survey used a KB of 179 ft; the 2.9 ft difference comes from the datum, so the sources agree.

benchmarks.q: Does the Marabooka 1 report suggest the Toolachee and Patchawarra could be in communication? Cite the evidence and state how sure the report is.
benchmarks.key: It raises communication as one possible explanation for the water-wet Patchawarra and leaves it untested (p. 32).

benchmarks.q: On seismic line 80-KBK, which shotpoint is closest to Marabooka 1?
benchmarks.key: About shotpoint 123: the velocity survey diagram shows the well between SP 122 and SP 124 on line 80-KBK, and the time section shows the derrick between SP 120 and SP 130.
